## What I found

The guard defends against a state the type system already rules out: `totalOf` is module-private, its parameter is typed `Order` (non-nullable under `strictNullChecks`), and both callers construct the object literal in the same file a few lines up. There is no sequence that reaches the `throw` without violating an invariant TypeScript already enforces. That is an impossible-state guard, so the answer is delete it — the record calls this **OBSOLETE**, a structural finding rather than a cost/benefit judgment.

## Why it matters

The branch is unreachable, so it can only be covered by a test that casts through `as any` to fabricate an argument the compiler forbids — either a fake test asserting a fake contract, or a permanent uncovered branch in the coverage report. Removing it costs nothing and closes the question structurally; leaving it keeps a line that teaches the next reader that `Order` might be nullable here, which invites the same guard at the next call site.

Two things this finding does *not* cover: the guard would not protect `order.lines` or `line.amount` anyway (a non-null `order` with a missing `lines` still throws a `TypeError` one line later), and the finding depends on nothing reaching these callers through an `as Order` cast, `any`, or unvalidated `JSON.parse`. Your description says the callers build the literals themselves, which settles it for this module.

## Do this first

1. Delete the three guard lines; the body becomes `return order.lines.reduce((sum, line) => sum + line.amount, 0);`.
2. Optional, to stop the pattern recurring rather than fixing this one instance: enable `@typescript-eslint/no-unnecessary-condition` (needs type-aware linting), which flags this class of dead comparison at build time.
3. If a real nullable `Order` ever arrives from a parse or network boundary, validate at that boundary, not here.

## What I did not check

- Whether any caller path actually launders an `any`/`as Order` into these two sites — closes with `rg -n "as Order|JSON\.parse|: any" <the module and its importers>`.
- Whether `Order.lines` is itself optional in the type, which would be a separate, real guard question — closes by reading the `Order` declaration.
- I did not read the file; this verdict rests entirely on the premises you stated.

```
Subject:        totalOf() null/undefined parameter guard (module-private TS function)
Mode:           Retrospective
Necessity:      Fail
Necessity note: §1a impossible-state guard / logically dead branch. `strictNullChecks` makes
                `order: Order` non-nullable; the function is module-private and both callers
                construct the literal in-module, so no trigger sequence exists. Not §1c: the
                invariant's canonical record is the type annotation, not this code.
Outcome evidence: not applicable
Decision:       OBSOLETE
Rationale:      The failure mode the guard prevents cannot occur under the module's own
                invariants, so it has no value for that mode — not low value. Worth scoring is
                skipped per §1/§6.1. Its only observable effect is an unreachable branch that
                can be covered only by a type-defeating cast.
Next action:    Delete the `if (order === null || order === undefined) throw` block.
Verification:   Not run (no file path supplied). Closes with `tsc --noEmit` plus
                `rg -n "as Order|JSON\.parse" <module + importers>` to confirm no cast-laundered
                input reaches the callers.
Minimal alt:    None needed — the `Order` annotation already documents the invariant.
Revisit when:   Not required. Reopens automatically if `totalOf` is exported, `strictNullChecks`
                is disabled, or a caller begins passing externally parsed data.
```
